name: Upholstered (bench, quilted and piped)
process: The bench body is built up over its frame and covered in the cloth, the top quilted into panels with piped seams and a piped edge; the pile of a velvet runs one way over every panel so the colour reads evenly.

museum.text: Backless, 2.4 x 0.6 m, 0.44 m high: an upholstered body in velvet of the bay's own colour, its top quilted in four panels with piped seams and a piped edge, on a dark fumed-oak plinth set back 40 mm.

pileRule.text: Velvet can be cut pile up or pile down, for more shine or more saturated colour.

surface.form: Soft domes between quilting lines; firm piped arrises; the cloth pulled smooth at the sides.

photograph: Four soft panels on top with shadowed seams; the piping a bright line; sides smooth and dark.

unverified.reason: The bench's inner build-up (webbing, springs or foam, wadding) is not specified by the design or a source read.
